header: Question and answer pairs, with one named person
lead: A standfirst carrying the portrait, the name and the role, then the conversation as headings and prose.
author: The interviewee

questions.title: Why is this not an accordion?
questions.bodytext: Because a conversation folded into a dozen closed drawers cannot be read straight through, cannot be printed, and cannot be found by the browser's own find-in-page — which is most of the reason anybody publishes an interview in the first place.

questions.title: How is a pair marked up?
questions.bodytext: Each question and its answer are one article: the question is a heading at level three and the answer is rich text. The question therefore heads its own answer rather than floating above an undifferentiated run of paragraphs.

questions.title: Why is the question set in the accent colour?
questions.bodytext: So it can be found by eye when skimming, without a quotation mark or a "Q:" that a screen reader would then have to read out as a letter. The heading level already carries the structure; the colour only helps the eye.

questions.title: What about the width field?
questions.bodytext: It sets the band, not the measure. The conversation stays at a reading width whatever room it is given, because an answer set across a full page stops reading as speech.
